summary: Sylvain Brocquet is a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the École Normale Supérieure (1980) and under Marie-Claude Porcher (~1990–1996), and held a post at Aix-Marseille University around 1997.

Sylvain Lévi (1863–1935) was a scholar in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études, University of Paris, Collège de France (1894–1935), and Maison Franco-Japonaise (1926–1928).

Sylvie Hureau is a scholar in Buddhist studies and sinology. She has held posts as maître de conférences at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (attested 2012) and as a research fellow at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

Sze-bong Tso specializes in Buddhist studies and sinology. He earned his PhD at the Australian National University (1977–1982), studying under doctoral supervisors Jan Willem de Jong and Tissa Rajapatirana.

Sándor Kőrösi Csoma (1784–1842) was a scholar of Tibetology and linguistics. He studied at Bethlen Gabor College, the University of Göttingen under Johann Gottfried Eichhorn and Johann Dominicus Fiorillo, and in Tibet, later serving as librarian at The Asiatic Society.
Søren Sørensen (1848–1902) was a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He held posts at Herlufsholm School (1876–1878) and the University of Copenhagen (~1887–1902).
Sāmaṇera Bodhesako (1939–1988) worked in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He founded Path Press and served as an editor at the Buddhist Publication Society.
Sīlaratano studied under Narada Maha Thera, Nyanaponika Thera, and Ajahn Maha Bua (~1977–2011).
Sōgen Asahina (1891–1979) was a scholar in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He studied at Nihon University and held a post at Kanagawa University.

T. Chandrasekharan worked in Indology, having studied as a pupil of S. Kuppuswami Sastri. He served as Professor of History of Sanskrit Language and Literature at Madras Sanskrit College (attested 1951).

T. Griffith Foulk specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Michigan (~1978–1987) under Luis O. Gómez, later teaching there (~1987–1995) and serving as Riggs Professor of Religion at Sarah Lawrence College.
T. K. V. Desikachar (1938–2016) worked in Indology and religious studies. He studied under Tirumalai Krishnamacharya (~1961–1989) and founded the Krishnamacharya Yoga Mandiram in 1976.

T. R. Chintamani was an Indology scholar who studied under S. Kuppuswami Sastri. He served as Senior Lecturer in Sanskrit at the University of Madras (attested 1938–1951) and was manager and correspondent for the Journal of Oriental Research.

T. R. V. Murti (1902–1986) worked in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned a D.Litt. at Banaras Hindu University under Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan and held posts at Oxford (~1949–1950), BHU (~1953–1967), and McMaster University (~1970–1972).
T. S. Srinivasa Sastri worked in Indology and philosophy. He held posts, including professor, at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (attested 1972, 1984–1992).
T. Shrinivas Shastri is an Indology scholar who held posts as Pandit and Professor at the Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (attested 1993, 2026).

T. V. Ramachandra Dikshitar was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He served as Principal of Madras Sanskrit College (attested 1938) and Professor of Advaita Vedānta at Banaras Hindu University (attested 1946).
T. V. Vasudeva is an Indology and philosophy scholar. He has served as an Editorial Committee member (attested 2001) and Deputy Director (attested 2026) at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute.

T. V. Venkatachala Sastry (born 1933) is an Indologist and linguist. Educated at the University of Mysore, he held lectureships at Rural College, St. Joseph's, and Osmania University, and was a professor at the University of Mysore (1984–1994).
T. Venkatacharya was an Indology scholar who held posts at the Italian Institute for the Middle and Far East and as Professor of East Asian Studies at the University of Toronto (attested 1971).
